data.title: Izakaya Alley and Ramen Shop
data.summary: 64 modular Japanese back alley models: floor, wall, storey and roof bays, a counter ramen shop with stools, hot line, boiling well and ticket machine, an izakaya front, lanterns, signboards, vending machines, crates, kegs, bins and services. Shutter, lids, drawer and fans move.
data.description: Everything needed to build a narrow modern Japanese back alley and trade out of both sides of it. The street itself is modular: 4 m tarmac floor slabs on four ports, kerb and gully sections, 4 m rendered wall bays, first floor bays plain or with a balcony and a drying rail, and parapet roof caps, all stacking on one storey datum so a two sided alley closes by construction. Two shopfronts sit in that run. The ramen shop is a counter shop with no dining room: an open 3.4 m bay under a three panel noren, a 2 m ported counter module, fixed stools, a four burner broth range with its stock pots, a noodle boiling well whose basket lifts out, a basket rack, a pass shelf, a prep bench with a drawer and a chopping board, a chest fridge with a lifting lid, a crockery rack of stacked bowls, a meal ticket machine with a blank key panel, a stainless canopy hood and the bowls, gyoza plates and caddies left on the counter. The izakaya opposite has a timber lattice frontage with a sliding leaf, a standing bar with a foot rail, a charcoal skewer grill, low tables, floor cushions, crate seats, a beer tap tower, glasses, a sake and tokkuri service, a keg stack, bottle and beer crates and an iced bottle bin. Around them is the alley: round and cylindrical paper lanterns and an 8 m ported lantern wire run, hanging signboards, a menu easel, an A frame, drinks, hot can and cigarette vending machines, a noodle delivery bicycle and a rack, waste bins, sorted bags, a mop bucket, a folding chair, traffic cone, potted plants, a puddle plate, an external stair, an extract duct run, a wall fan, a condenser, a meter box and a utility pole with a 12 m cable span. Clips are rigid node transforms only: the shutter runs up its guides, the lattice leaf slides, bin and fridge lids open and close, the prep drawer runs out, the noodle basket lifts out of the well, vending flaps swing up, extract and condenser fans spin and the delivery bicycle rolls. The noren, the overhead cables, the drying laundry, the refuse bags, the charcoal, the broth and the steam are modelled solid and stated static, because flexible and fluid material needs a joint per element that one rigid node cannot give; the folding chair and the A frame do not fold for the same reason, and there are no people, because the pack has no skinned meshes. Nothing here carries a real mark: every sign face, noren, lantern, can, bottle, keg, crate, shutter and machine front is blank or dressed with invented abstract shapes, there is no lettering in any script, and no colourway copies a real product. Original AI-generated CC0 geometry, prepared for human review. No physics, gameplay, colliders, navigation or embedded lights.

starterScene.description: A 24 m by 16 m back alley trading at opening time, laid in one continuous tarmac surface with kerbs and gully grates down both sides. A counter ramen shop opens onto the west side through two 4 m bays under an indigo noren: an 8 m counter with eight stools facing the street, a four burner hot line with the stock pots on it under a stainless hood, a noodle boiling well with the basket in it, a basket rack, a prep bench, a chest fridge, a crockery rack, a meal ticket machine and bowls, gyoza and caddies left along the counter. Opposite, an izakaya behind a sliding lattice screen has put a standing bar, a charcoal skewer grill, two low tables with cushions and its crates, kegs and iced bottles out into the alley. Both sides carry a shuttered unit, one open and one closed, a vending machine row, signboards, lanterns on three spans of wire down the middle, an external stair to a first floor balcony with the washing out, extract ducts, condensers and the overhead cables between two utility poles.
